Gold "The only safe asset when bonds betray you" 
 Why retail is here: The narrative is viscerally simple: Treasuries — the supposed risk-free asset — are in revolt.
The 10-year yield is surging (4.74% and climbing), the 30-year has breached levels that headlines call a "structural shift," and bond market turmoil is dominating every financial news cycle.
Mohamed El-Erian flagged the 30-year yield at 5.27% as a "structural shift." The Gold/Copper ratio at 711 is tagged "FEAR-elevated," confirming this is a haven bid, not a broad commodity reflation.
The bond selloff — with the 10Y yield rising 1.3% over four weeks and the 10Y-2Y spread blowing out to +103bps — is the direct accelerant.
Every basis point higher in yields without an equity crash reinforces the narrative that something is fundamentally wrong with sovereign debt, and gold is the exit.

The key mechanical similarity to Bitcoin 2020 is that the asset is being treated as a referendum on government competence rather than priced on traditional fundamentals like real yields or opportunity cost — which is precisely what makes these trades both powerful and eventually fragile.

However, professionals note the paradox: gold is surging even as real yields rise (the 10Y at 4.74% with inflation trending toward target implies strongly positive real rates), which historically should suppress gold.
Specifically, if the new Fed Chair Warsh signals credible fiscal-monetary coordination that pulls the 30-year yield back below 5%, the panic bid in gold evaporates overnight.
A successful Treasury auction cycle with strong demand would have the same effect.

Alternatively, if rising yields finally crack equities hard enough to trigger a genuine risk-off event (the Dow already tumbled 700 points mid-week), forced liquidation of gold positions to meet margin calls could trigger a vicious 8–12% drawdown in days — exactly as happened in March 2020.

The risk is a "sell the news" reaction if guidance merely meets expectations rather than exceeds them, or if bond market stress finally spills over into the duration-sensitive growth trade — the 10Y at 4.74% and climbing is a silent tax on every AI stock's discounted cash flow model.
